claim: Clothing and jewelry commonly contain computers.
originalWording: Clothing and jewelry commonly contain computers.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 3, printed pp. 12–13

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Computing in wearable body ornaments is a common product/use category; watches count and every example need not be equally adopted.
reference.rationale: Wearable and embedded devices existed, but the 2009 common-use threshold was only partly reached. By the June 2019 US survey, 21% regularly wore a smartwatch or fitness tracker. That is common, not universal; it supports a late wearable-form-factor success.

evidence.title: Pew: About one-in-five Americans use a smartwatch or fitness tracker
evidence.note: June 2019 US survey: 21% regularly wear one. Common does not mean majority, and US adult prevalence is not global prevalence.. June 2019 US survey: 21% regularly wear one. Common does not mean majority, and US adult prevalence is not global prevalence.

strict.criterion: Both everyday clothing and a broad range of jewelry commonly embed computers.
strict.rationale: Smartwatches satisfy part of the list, but broadly computerized clothing and the full jewelry assortment are not comparably established.
